meta.caveats: Counts for Moga are anchored on the DIC/MSME-DI 2010-11 profile (s1) and scaled to 2026 with population (~1.1M Moga district, ~2.6M tricity urban) and per-capita density heuristics; every figure marked 'est.' in notes is a modelling estimate, not an official statistic. Revenues in INR per establishment per year.

sectors.name: Arhtiyas (commission agents, grain mandis)
sectors.paymentTerms: Govt agencies pay MSP directly into farmer bank accounts since Rabi 2021 (PFMS/DBT); arhtiya commission (~Rs 46/qtl) paid by agency to arhtiya account; labour charges reimbursed per bag; side lending and input sales settled in cash/khata at harvest
sectors.creditPractice: Core rural lender: running khata per farmer family, advances for inputs, weddings, medical, tractor down-payments; interest commonly 1-1.5%/month (12-18% p.a.), reports up to 18-37%; loan recovered by netting against harvest proceeds (now via farmer handing over payment after DBT). Farmers owe arhtiyas an estimated Rs 17,000-20,000 cr statewide
sectors.seasonality: Two procurement peaks: wheat 1 Apr-31 May, paddy 1 Oct-30 Nov (90% of commission income); lending peaks Jun-Sep and Dec-Mar
sectors.notes: Punjab: ~47,000 licences but ~20,232 operating families (PAU study) and ~24,000-28,000 licensed active. Moga ~5-6% of state procurement -> est. 1,800-2,000 licences, ~1,100 active firms. Commission was 2.5% of MSP (since 1998) but frozen by Centre at ~Rs 45.88/qtl (~1.8-1.9% of MSP now). Moga throughput est. ~20 LMT wheat+paddy -> ~Rs 95 cr commission/yr district-wide (~Rs 85 lakh/firm) plus interest income and labour-contract margin. Revenue figure = commission + interest + margin, not grain turnover (grain value passing through a typical firm ~Rs 45-55 cr).

sectors.name: Rice shellers / mills (custom milling + private basmati)
sectors.paymentTerms: Custom-milled rice delivered to FCI against agency-allotted paddy; milling charges and byproduct sale; private basmati bought cash/RTGS via arhtiyas, sold to exporters on 30-60 day credit
sectors.creditPractice: Bank working-capital limits (CC) secured on plant; bank guarantee/security to state agency for paddy held in custody; delayed FCI acceptance and storage-space crunch tie up capital for months; heavy reliance on arhtiya relationships for private paddy
sectors.seasonality: Paddy intake Oct-Dec; milling and CMR delivery Dec-Jun (deadlines often extended to Sep); idle in monsoon
sectors.notes: Punjab ~5,500 shelling units (Punjab Rice Industry Assn ~5,520); 4,132 allotted paddy in KMS 2024-25. Average allotment ~4,000-4,500 t paddy/miller (175 LMT/4,132). Moga share est. ~5% -> ~260 units (DIC 2010-11 lists 445 food-product units incl. shellers, spice, dairy). Revenue mix (est.): byproducts (bran ~7%, husk ~22%, broken), milling charge, private basmati trading. Gross margin thin and volatile; outturn 67% norm is a recurring dispute.

sectors.name: Village flour chakkis / small atta mills
sectors.paymentTerms: Cash or UPI per pisai (grinding) job; households bring own wheat
sectors.creditPractice: Small udhaar for regular households; settled monthly
sectors.seasonality: Steady; spikes before festivals and weddings
sectors.notes: Est. ~4 per village x 323 villages + ~200 urban. Many run on PSPCL agricultural/commercial power. Revenue is grinding fees (~Rs 3-5/kg) plus some packed atta sales.

sectors.name: Roller flour mills (maida, sooji, atta) / packed atta
sectors.paymentTerms: Wheat bought from FCI OMSS e-auctions (RTGS advance) or private trade; sells to distributors on 15-30 day credit
sectors.creditPractice: Distributor credit 15-30 days; bank CC limits
sectors.notes: Est. ~8 in Moga district and ~17 in Mohali/Panchkula/Derabassi belt. Tricity bakery/HoReCa demand drives maida.

sectors.name: Cold stores (potato, fruit/veg, dairy)
sectors.paymentTerms: Rent per bag/quintal per season; collected at withdrawal; part cash
sectors.creditPractice: Store owners advance loans to farmers/traders against stored stock (pledge), ~1-1.5%/month
sectors.notes: DIC 2010-11: 26 cold storage/aux units, Rs 18.5 cr investment, 178 employees. Est. 30-40 now. Cold storage listed as potential new-MSME area.

sectors.name: Seed / fertilizer / pesticide dealers
sectors.paymentTerms: Fertilizer at fixed MRP via PoS (Aadhaar-authenticated); pesticides and seed often on udhaar until harvest; UPI growing for cash sales
sectors.creditPractice: Crop-cycle credit: farmer settles after wheat (May) or paddy (Nov); implicit interest via higher price or 1.5-2%/month; tie-in sales (urea with unwanted products) reported during shortages
sectors.seasonality: Peaks Oct-Dec (wheat sowing: DAP) and Jun-Aug (paddy: urea, zinc, herbicides)
sectors.notes: Est. ~2.3 per village. Many arhtiyas also run input shops, so input credit and grain sale are netted on the same khata. PACS (cooperatives) sell ~40-50% of fertilizer in Punjab (est.).

sectors.name: Tractor & implement dealerships
sectors.paymentTerms: Down-payment 15-25% cash/UPI; balance via bank/NBFC tractor loan (half-yearly instalments aligned to harvests)
sectors.creditPractice: Dealer gives short credit on spares/service; trade-ins of old tractors common
sectors.seasonality: Sales peak Mar-Apr and Sep-Oct (pre-harvest, after paddy payments), Dhanteras/Diwali
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~800-1,000 new tractors/yr. Brands: Mahindra/Swaraj (Swaraj made in Mohali), Sonalika, John Deere, New Holland, Eicher, Farmtrac. Punjab has very high tractor density (over-capitalisation widely noted).

sectors.name: Agricultural implement / combine-part manufacturers (Focal Point cluster)
sectors.paymentTerms: Cash/UPI and cheques; dealer credit 30-60 days
sectors.creditPractice: Farmers often pay part after harvest; subsidy-linked sales (CRM machines: Happy Seeder, super-SMS) paid partly via subsidy DBT to farmer
sectors.seasonality: Pre-season Aug-Oct (straw management, seed drills) and Feb-Mar
sectors.notes: DIC 2010-11: NIC-29 machinery & equipment 445 units, 3,182 employees, Rs 26 cr output; identified cluster: Agriculture Implements, Focal Point Moga (215 plots).

sectors.name: Farm machinery & tubewell repair workshops / mechanics
sectors.paymentTerms: Cash/UPI; udhaar for known farmers
sectors.creditPractice: Bills settled at harvest; 1-3 month udhaar common
sectors.seasonality: Peaks just before and during harvests
sectors.notes: Est. DIC lists 117 registered motor-vehicle repair units (2010-11); unregistered repair dominates. Est. 2-3 per village.

sectors.name: Combine harvester / custom hiring operators
sectors.paymentTerms: Per-acre charge (~Rs 1,800-2,500/acre wheat/paddy, est.) cash or after sale of crop
sectors.creditPractice: Many paid after crop sale; some combines migrate to other states seasonally
sectors.notes: Est. Includes self-propelled combines and Happy Seeder/baler hire. Revenue/margins sensitive to diesel price.

sectors.name: Village milk collection centres (Nestle VCCs, Verka/Milkfed societies, private dodhis)
sectors.paymentTerms: Farmers paid every 10-15 days by bank transfer (Nestle, Verka) based on fat/SNF; dodhis pay cash weekly
sectors.creditPractice: Advances to farmers for cattle purchase/feed recovered from milk bills; dodhis lend informally
sectors.seasonality: Flush season Nov-Mar (+30-40% volume), lean Apr-Jul
sectors.notes: Nestle: >1.3-1.5 million kg/day in flush from >110,000 farmers across catchment; ~2,815 collection centres nationally; Kaonke Kalan example ~75 farmers, ~1,000 L/day. Moga has 245k buffaloes, 92k cows (2011). Est. ~2 centres per village.

sectors.name: Factory ancillary vendors, Moga (packaging, engineering maintenance, cattle feed, contract services)
sectors.paymentTerms: Invoiced with GST; 30-60 day credit from Nestle; e-invoicing
sectors.creditPractice: Bank bill discounting/TReDS sometimes; formal
sectors.seasonality: Steady; milk tanker volumes follow flush season
sectors.notes: Anchor buyer is Nestle India's Moga factory (only large unit in DIC profile; milk collection began 1961; the sim instantiates it as its own agent, so it is NOT listed as a sector here). DIC 2010-11: all large+medium units Rs 1,554 cr turnover, 1,699 employees. DIC: 'setting up of a few large units can boost ancillarisation' - ancillary base is thin; est. 40-80 registered vendors in district. Also includes milk-tanker contractors.

sectors.name: Truck owner-operators (1-3 trucks)
sectors.paymentTerms: Paid per trip by booking agent/transport company: 70-90% advance or on delivery, balance 15-45 days after POD; mandi/grain work paid after govt reimbursement (can lag months)
sectors.creditPractice: Truck bought on NBFC loan (Shriram, etc.) 14-18% p.a.; diesel credit at local pump settled monthly
sectors.seasonality: Peak demand Apr-Jun (wheat) and Oct-Jan (paddy, CMR); lean monsoon
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~2,000 goods trucks (HGV/MGV) + tractor-trolleys; tricity ~1,500 truck-owning operators using Transport Nagar Chandigarh/Mohali/Zirakpur. Most owners hold 1-3 trucks. Former truck-union (cartel) members.

sectors.name: Transport companies / booking agents (Transport Nagar)
sectors.paymentTerms: Bilty (LR) issued; consignor pays 'to pay' or 'paid'; credit 15-45 days to regular clients; commission 5-10% on hired trucks
sectors.creditPractice: Advance diesel/cash to drivers; carry receivables of industry
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~150, tricity ~550 (Chandigarh Transport Area Sec 26/Indl Area, Mohali Phase, Zirakpur).

sectors.name: Mandi labour & cartage (transport) contractors
sectors.paymentTerms: Paid by state agencies/FCI against tendered schedule-of-rates (+% premium cap); payment lag 1-6 months
sectors.creditPractice: Need security deposits (~Rs 5/t cluster capacity); front labour wages and diesel
sectors.notes: Cluster-wise annual tenders by Punjab Food & Civil Supplies (Transportation Policy). Since 2017-18 open tendering; where no bids after 3 attempts, arhtiyas/shellers allowed to bid. Labour: Rs ~16-19.26 per bag paid via contractors; palledar complaints of underpayment.

sectors.name: Petrol pumps (Moga district)
sectors.paymentTerms: OMC paid in advance (RTGS); retail UPI/cash/card; farmers and truckers on monthly diesel credit
sectors.creditPractice: Diesel udhaar to farmers repaid at harvest; truck fleets monthly
sectors.seasonality: Diesel peaks at harvest/sowing and paddy transplanting (Jun)
sectors.notes: Est. Punjab ~3,800-4,000 outlets x ~4.5% (Moga). Margin is fixed dealer commission (~Rs 2-4/L). Punjab diesel Rs 95.59 vs Chandigarh Rs 89.47 (Oct 2026) - trucks fill in Chandigarh when possible.

sectors.name: Petrol pumps (Chandigarh, Mohali, Panchkula)
sectors.paymentTerms: UPI/card dominant; fleet cards
sectors.creditPractice: Corporate/fleet credit monthly
sectors.notes: Est. Chandigarh ~45, Mohali district ~100, Panchkula ~45. Chandigarh's lower VAT pulls fuel demand from Mohali/Zirakpur/Panchkula.

sectors.name: Highway dhabas & roadside eateries
sectors.paymentTerms: Cash/UPI; truckers sometimes on account
sectors.creditPractice: Supplier credit 7-15 days from wholesaler
sectors.seasonality: Steady; spikes on weekends and harvest truck traffic
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~250 (NH-5/NH-703, Moga-Kotkapura, Moga-Barnala) and ~200 on Kharar-Ludhiana/Zirakpur-Banur belts.

sectors.name: Kiryana / general stores (Moga)
sectors.paymentTerms: Cash + UPI (QR now ubiquitous); 'khata' (udhaar) for regular households
sectors.creditPractice: Udhaar for 20-40% of customers in villages (est.), settled monthly by salaried households and at harvest by farm households; wholesaler gives the shop 7-21 days credit
sectors.seasonality: Spikes after harvest payments (May, Nov) and during Diwali/weddings
sectors.notes: Est. ~1 per 32 households (~210k households). Most unregistered for GST (below Rs 40 lakh threshold or composition scheme).

sectors.name: Kiryana / convenience stores (tricity)
sectors.paymentTerms: UPI dominant, cards; khata for known residents
sectors.creditPractice: Monthly khata for salaried families; quick-commerce competition reduces credit power
sectors.notes: Est. Chandigarh city has ~40,000 shops/establishments of which only ~13,900 registered with Labour Dept; quick commerce (Blinkit/Zepto/Instamart) present in tricity.

sectors.name: Wholesale traders & FMCG distributors (staples, packaged goods)
sectors.paymentTerms: FMCG companies need advance/RTGS; wholesaler gives retailers 7-21 days credit; cash discounts for immediate pay
sectors.creditPractice: Credit lines to retailers tracked in books/apps; collection rounds weekly
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~150 (Main Bazar, New Town), tricity ~450 (Grain Market Sec 26 Chandigarh, Mohali Phase, Zirakpur). Ludhiana is the regional C&F hub feeding both.

sectors.name: Cloth & readymade garment wholesale/retail (incl. Ludhiana hosiery resale)
sectors.paymentTerms: Retail cash/UPI; wholesale 'dhara' credit 30-90 days from Ludhiana/Amritsar suppliers
sectors.creditPractice: Long trade credit chains; wedding-season bulk purchases by families sometimes on udhaar
sectors.seasonality: Weddings Oct-Feb, festivals (Diwali, Lohri), winterwear from Ludhiana Sep-Dec
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~700, tricity ~1,500. DIC: apparel 28 units, textile 8 (manufacturing negligible in Moga; hosiery is Ludhiana).

sectors.name: Jewellers (gold, wedding jewellery)
sectors.paymentTerms: Mixed cash/RTGS/UPI; PAN mandatory above Rs 2 lakh cash; old-gold exchange common; hallmarking (HUID)
sectors.creditPractice: Gold savings schemes (11-month); some lend against gold (informal)
sectors.seasonality: Wedding season Oct-Feb, Akshaya Tritiya, Dhanteras; NRI visit season Dec-Jan
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~400, tricity ~900. NRI remittances heavily fund wedding gold in Moga/Doaba-Malwa belt.

sectors.name: IELTS / PTE coaching centres
sectors.paymentTerms: Upfront course fees (Rs 8,000-20,000, est.) via UPI/cash; exam fees paid to IDP/British Council online
sectors.creditPractice: Instalment plans; little credit
sectors.notes: Moga is a known IELTS hub; directory lists 47 IELTS centres (s44) but local estimates historically 200-300+. Canada's 2024 study-permit caps and SDS end cut Punjab enrolment 70-80% at some centres and closed ~30% of centres. Licensed under Punjab Prevention of Human Smuggling/Travel Professions Regulation Act 2012/2014.

sectors.name: Immigration consultants, visa & travel agents
sectors.paymentTerms: Fees in tranches (file opening, offer letter, visa); university commissions from abroad (forex inflow); tickets on cards/UPI
sectors.creditPractice: Families fund study abroad via land sale/mortgage, education loans, arhtiya/relative loans; agents sometimes hold passports/fees as leverage
sectors.seasonality: Tied to foreign intakes and NRI season (Nov-Jan)
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~250, tricity ~850 (Mohali alone had 471 registered travel agents; Sector 17/34 Chandigarh). Regular DC licence cancellations (e.g. 263 in Jalandhar). Demand shifting from Canada to Germany/France/Ireland/Australia.

sectors.name: Private schools
sectors.paymentTerms: Monthly/quarterly fees via bank/UPI; transport fees separate
sectors.creditPractice: Fee arrears tolerated for a term; farm households pay after harvest
sectors.seasonality: Admissions Mar-Apr; fee peaks Apr and Oct
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~400 private schools (2010: 403 primary + 374 middle/high/senior-secondary across all managements), tricity ~600 incl. high-fee CBSE schools.

sectors.name: Coaching institutes / tuition (JEE/NEET/govt jobs/computer)
sectors.paymentTerms: Upfront/instalment fees, UPI
sectors.creditPractice: Instalments
sectors.notes: Est. Sector 34 Chandigarh coaching hub ~500 institutes; Moga ~300 (DIC lists coaching among services).

sectors.name: Private hospitals, nursing homes & clinics
sectors.paymentTerms: Cash/UPI/cards upfront; cashless via insurers and Ayushman Bharat/Mukh Mantri Sehat Bima (reimbursed 30-90 days)
sectors.creditPractice: Families borrow from arhtiyas/relatives for surgery; pharma distributors give 30-60 days
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~250 (2011: 1 govt district hospital, 5 CHCs, 22 PHCs, 53 dispensaries), tricity ~1,450 incl. PGIMER, GMCH-32, Fortis Mohali, Max Mohali, Alchemist Panchkula.

sectors.name: Chemists / pharmacies
sectors.paymentTerms: Cash/UPI; distributors give 30-45 days
sectors.creditPractice: Small udhaar to regulars
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~800, tricity ~2,500. Panchkula/Baddi pharma belt supplies.

sectors.name: Commercial & cooperative bank branches
sectors.paymentTerms: KCC (crop loans ~7% with subvention), CC limits, NRI deposit accounts
sectors.creditPractice: KCC renewed annually; NPAs high in agriculture; arhtiyas often route farmer payments
sectors.notes: Moga had 166 branches in 2010 (SBI 16, SBOP 11, PNB 15, others 77, cooperative 47); est. ~260 now. Tricity est. ~1,050 (Chandigarh ~500). Large NRI deposit base in Moga. Revenue = est. net interest + fee income per branch (~Rs 100 cr book x ~3% spread).

sectors.name: Primary agricultural cooperative societies (PACS)
sectors.paymentTerms: Short-term crop loans in kind (fertilizer) and cash; recovery after harvest
sectors.creditPractice: Members borrow up to limit; defaults rolled over; fertilizer at MRP
sectors.notes: Est. Punjab ~3,500 PACS; Moga ~190. Central Cooperative Bank Moga branches funded them.

sectors.name: Moneylenders, MFIs & NBFC lenders
sectors.paymentTerms: Weekly/monthly cash or UPI collection; JLG loans fortnightly
sectors.creditPractice: Informal 2-3%/month; MFI ~22-26% p.a.; NBFC vehicle loans 14-18%
sectors.seasonality: Demand peaks in lean months and before weddings
sectors.notes: Est. Arhtiyas are the main informal lender to landed farmers (>1/5 of rural debt to arhtiyas+moneylenders, per PARI); MFIs/NBFCs serve labourers and women's groups.

sectors.name: Real estate developers & brokers (Mohali/New Chandigarh/Zirakpur/Kharar)
sectors.paymentTerms: Construction-linked plans via bank home loans; cash component in resale land deals; RERA escrow 70%
sectors.creditPractice: Developer funding from NBFCs/private credit; buyers from NRI remittances
sectors.notes: Est. incl. brokers. Mohali/Kharar/Zirakpur growth absorbs Punjab rural savings and NRI money from Moga-Malwa belt.

sectors.name: Construction firms, masons & building-material dealers (cement, steel, hardware)
sectors.paymentTerms: Stage payments; cash wages to (often migrant) labour weekly
sectors.creditPractice: Dealers give 30-60 day credit to contractors
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~1,000, tricity ~2,000. Dealers sell cement, steel, sanitaryware.

sectors.name: Brick kilns
sectors.paymentTerms: Advance (peshgi) to migrant labour families recovered from per-1,000-brick piece rates; buyers cash/UPI on delivery
sectors.creditPractice: Labour advance-debt bondage risk; buyers credit 15-30 days
sectors.notes: Punjab ~2,700 kilns (2014); Moga named among districts with most kilns. Est. 100-120 in Moga (DIC: non-metallic mineral products 120 units, 3,608 employees, 2010-11).

sectors.name: Car, two-wheeler & commercial vehicle dealers
sectors.paymentTerms: Bank/NBFC finance + down-payment; cash/UPI for small; trade-in
sectors.creditPractice: Floor-plan credit from OEM-linked banks
sectors.seasonality: Navratri-Diwali, Baisakhi, post-harvest; SUVs very popular
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~50, tricity ~150.

sectors.name: Mobile phone & consumer electronics retail/repair
sectors.paymentTerms: UPI/cash; consumer-durable EMI (Bajaj Finserv etc.)
sectors.creditPractice: NBFC 0% EMI pervasive; shop gives little credit
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~700, tricity ~1,500. DIC flags mobile repair as a service potential.

sectors.name: Restaurants, cafes, sweet shops (halwais), bakeries
sectors.paymentTerms: UPI/cards; Zomato/Swiggy settle weekly minus commission
sectors.creditPractice: Suppliers 7-30 days
sectors.seasonality: Weekends, festivals; Chandigarh nightlife; halwais peak Diwali/weddings
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~700, tricity ~3,300 (Sector 7/8/26/35 Chandigarh, Mohali Phase 3B2/7, Zirakpur).

sectors.name: IT / ITES firms (Chandigarh IT Park, Mohali Quark City/IT City)
sectors.paymentTerms: Invoiced with GST/LUT for exports; salaries via bank monthly
sectors.creditPractice: Formal; receivables 30-90 days from clients
sectors.notes: Punjab: 150+ registered IT units, ~35,000 professionals (Mohali), Quark City 70+ IT/ITeS firms; Infosys Chandigarh ~6,000 staff; plus Tech Mahindra, Teleperformance, TaskUs. Est. tricity IT/ITES employment ~70,000-90,000.

sectors.name: Government employers (UT admin, Punjab & Haryana secretariats, central offices, PGIMER, PU, police, courts)
sectors.paymentTerms: Monthly salaries/pensions via bank (1st of month)
sectors.creditPractice: Salary-backed personal loans; government employees are the most creditworthy kiryana khata customers
sectors.seasonality: Steady; DA hikes, pay commission arrears are demand shocks
sectors.notes: Aggregate employer (count=1). Est. ~150,000 serving employees and large pensioner base; drives tricity consumption and housing demand.

sectors.name: Government employers (Punjab govt teachers, police, PSPCL, district offices)
sectors.paymentTerms: Monthly salary via bank
sectors.creditPractice: Salary-backed loans
sectors.notes: Aggregate employer (count=1). Est. ~15,000 employees in district; 2010 had 403 primary, 374 secondary-level schools, 22 PHCs, 5 CHCs.

sectors.name: Hotels & guest houses
sectors.paymentTerms: OTA (MakeMyTrip/Booking) settle 7-30 days; corporate credit; GST invoices
sectors.creditPractice: Corporate 30-day credit
sectors.seasonality: Wedding season, conferences, Shimla-bound tourists through Chandigarh
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~40, tricity ~290.

sectors.name: Marriage palaces, banquet halls, caterers, tent houses, DJs, decorators
sectors.paymentTerms: Booking advance 20-30%, balance on the day in cash/RTGS; large cash component
sectors.creditPractice: Families fund weddings from harvest money, NRI remittances, arhtiya loans
sectors.seasonality: Oct-Mar (auspicious dates), Feb peak; NRI weddings Dec-Feb
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~350 (incl. GT-road marriage palaces, caterers), tricity ~550. Punjabi weddings among most expensive in India relative to income.

sectors.name: Gurdwaras & religious-trust economy (langar, kar seva, shops)
sectors.paymentTerms: Donations (cash, UPI QR, wheat/milk in kind); bulk purchases of atta, dal, ghee, LPG
sectors.creditPractice: Not credit-based; donations surge at harvest and gurpurabs
sectors.seasonality: Gurpurab (Nov), Baisakhi (Apr), Hola Mohalla; harvest-time donations
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~550 gurdwaras (1-2 per village + town), tricity ~350. Langar is a significant B2B buyer of staples and a safety-net food source.

sectors.name: E-commerce & quick-commerce delivery hubs (Amazon, Flipkart, Delhivery, Blinkit and Zepto dark stores)
sectors.paymentTerms: Platform pays hub/franchise per parcel; COD collected in cash/UPI then remitted
sectors.creditPractice: Riders paid weekly per drop
sectors.notes: Est. Moga ~25 hubs (COD share high), tricity ~135 incl. ~60 quick-commerce dark stores. Riders ~10-15 per hub.

sectors.name: Fruit & vegetable wholesale mandi traders (Sec 26 Chandigarh, Mohali Phase 11, Moga sabzi mandi)
sectors.paymentTerms: Farmers paid cash/UPI same day minus commission (~4-6%, est.); retail vendors buy on daily credit
sectors.creditPractice: Daily/weekly running credit to rehri vendors
sectors.notes: Est.

sectors.name: Ration depots (PDS under NFSA)
sectors.paymentTerms: Free wheat under PMGKAY; dealer margin per qtl from govt
sectors.creditPractice: Govt margin delays
sectors.notes: Est. Punjab ~18,000 depots x ~4.5%.

sectors.name: Organised manufacturing (Mohali, Derabassi, Panchkula, Chandigarh Industrial Area)
sectors.paymentTerms: GST invoices, 30-90 day credit, MSME 45-day rule (Sec 43B(h))
sectors.creditPractice: Bank CC limits; TReDS
sectors.notes: Est. Products: tractors, auto parts, pharma, electronics, chemicals. Incl. Swaraj tractors (Mahindra, Mohali), Chandigarh Industrial Area Ph I/II, Mohali Phases, Derabassi pharma/chemicals, Panchkula. Chandigarh GST base ~33,800 registered taxpayers (Jun 2026).

sectors.name: Hosiery & garment small units / tailoring
sectors.paymentTerms: Job-work paid weekly cash; wholesale credit 60-90 days
sectors.creditPractice: Long credit chains to Ludhiana
sectors.notes: Moga is not a hosiery cluster (DIC: 28 apparel units); Ludhiana (60 km) is. Mostly boutiques/tailors (DIC lists designer boutiques as potential).
